channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Introduces New Treatment Protocols for Major Diseases
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has developed over 60 algorithms for diagnosing and treating cardiovascular, kidney, and oncological diseases, as well as emergency care. These new protocols are being implemented across all medical facilities nationwide. Training sessions are underway for medical staff, with online options available for doctors in other regions, aiming to improve timely and quality medical care for all citizens.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Selling SIM Cards and Bank Accounts Leads to Criminal Charges
item.description: Cybercrime is on the rise in Kyrgyzstan, with traditional street crimes declining. The Osh city prosecutor's office has opened 52 criminal cases related to the intentional transfer or sale of electronic payment means, virtual asset wallets, and SIM cards. Authorities are increasingly prosecuting individuals who facilitate remote fraud schemes by selling their SIM cards or opening accounts for criminals, highlighting the shift from physical to digital crime.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy to Grow Fastest in Central Asia, ADB Forecasts
item.description: The Asian Development Bank forecasts Kyrgyzstan's economy to grow by 8.9% in 2026, outpacing other Central Asian nations. Growth is supported by state investments, consumption, and construction, despite a widening current account deficit and weakening trade. Tajikistan and Uzbekistan are projected to grow by 7.0%, Turkmenistan by 6.3%, and Kazakhstan by 4.8%.

item.title: Kyrgyz Potatoes to Be Exported to Uzbekistan Without Obstacles Following Agreement
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan have agreed to expand mutual trade in agricultural products and improve market access for Kyrgyz producers. The agreement, discussed by the agriculture ministers, ensures uninterrupted supply and export of Kyrgyz potatoes to Uzbekistan. Procedures for registering Kyrgyz agricultural processing enterprises in Uzbekistan and establishing joint ventures were also expedited.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Birth Rate Declines for Fifth Consecutive Year Post-Pandemic
item.description: The number of births in Kazakhstan has decreased for the fifth year in a row since the pandemic. In January-September 2026, 226,990 children were born, a significant drop from previous years. The total fertility rate has fallen to 14.74 per 1,000 people, continuing a downward trend that began after a peak in 2021.

item.title: Industrial Kostanay Region Faces Labor Shortages Despite Agricultural and Industrial Output
item.description: Kostanay region in Kazakhstan, a major producer of wheat and automobiles, is experiencing labor shortages. Environmentalists are concerned about soil degradation, while activists highlight low incomes and the influence of Russian propaganda. The region's proximity to Russia significantly impacts its economy, trade, migration, and daily life.

item.title: Kazakhstan Struggles with Youth Recruitment into Drug Trafficking Schemes
item.description: Young people in Kazakhstan are increasingly being lured into dangerous drug trafficking activities through online advertisements promising easy money. Many are caught acting as couriers, facing criminal charges. Last year, 67 minors were prosecuted, and 59 this year. The Prosecutor's Office reported 8,280 drug-related crimes last year.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine Fail to Reach Agreement in Abu Dhabi Peace Talks
item.description: Two-day peace talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US in Abu Dhabi concluded without a concrete agreement to halt the conflict. US representatives plan to meet with Vladimir Putin in Moscow and Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin. Despite challenges due to Russia's rigid stance, Ukrainian representatives noted positive momentum and proposed an early next meeting.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Audit Chamber Reviews Science Funding Effectiveness
item.description: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber presented findings on the effectiveness of science funding, noting a 2.4-fold increase in R&D spending to 261.5 billion tenge between 2021-2025. Despite increased funding, science's role in the economy has not significantly improved, with 74% of R&D expenses covered by the state budget. A unified system for project accounting is lacking.

item.title: Bishkek Prepares 114 Units of Equipment for Snow Removal
item.description: Bishkek has prepared 114 special vehicles and work crews from the 'Tazalyk' municipal enterprise for anticipated snowfall. The fleet includes snowplows, tractors, loaders, and dump trucks. Road service personnel and street cleaners will also be involved in clearing operations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Trade with Netherlands Shifts: Coal Exports Rise, Oil Declines
item.description: Kazakhstan's bilateral trade with the Netherlands decreased by 3.6% in January-September 2026. While oil exports fell, shipments of coal surged nearly fivefold. Other exports like tires and plywood also increased, while imports from the Netherlands saw a significant reduction.

item.title: Naryn City Heating Season: 30 Boiler Houses Supplying Heat
item.description: In Naryn city, 30 boiler houses are currently providing heat to the population and socio-economic facilities. The municipality reports that all boiler houses are operating according to requirements, with any issues being resolved promptly. The heating season is under the city mayor's supervision.

item.title: Four Central Asian Nations to Establish Electricity Trading Platform
item.description: Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan plan to create a joint trading platform for electricity. The Coordination Dispatch Center 'Energiya' has launched an international tender for a pilot short-term market, supported by the World Bank. This initiative aims to facilitate the buying and selling of electricity on a day-ahead basis, complementing existing long-term contracts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ready to Host CSTO Events in 2027, President Japarov States
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov announced Kyrgyzstan's readiness to host Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) events in 2027 during a meeting in Moscow. He emphasized strengthening collective security and cooperation, highlighting Kyrgyzstan's participation in joint military exercises. Japarov also addressed counter-terrorism, drug trafficking, and the situation in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Moldova Discuss Trade, Investment, and Energy Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov met with Moldova's Prime Minister Vasile Tofan to discuss trade, economic cooperation, investment, and energy sector collaboration. Both leaders expressed interest in expanding mutual trade and developing transport and logistics links, including the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route. Moldova noted Kazakhstan's progressive economic reforms and strengthened position in the energy market.

item.title: Bishkek Authorities Hold Open Dialogue with Parents on Child Safety
item.description: Interdepartmental meetings are underway in Bishkek to ensure child safety, prevent offenses, and protect their health. City officials, school principals, and parents participated in a recent session. Representatives from various agencies provided information on preventing juvenile delinquency and safeguarding children's well-being.

item.title: Kazakhstan Boosts Rural Healthcare with Significant Investment and New Facilities
item.description: Kazakhstan is prioritizing accessible medical care in rural areas, a key aspect of its national policy. Over the past seven years, 1,259 medical facilities have been built, primarily in villages. President Tokayev highlighted that 88 trillion tenge has been allocated to social development, improving healthcare quality across all regions, especially in remote settlements. Citizens are entitled to over a thousand types of free medical services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Export Potatoes to Uzbekistan Without Restrictions
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan are set to expand agricultural trade, develop joint processing enterprises, and remove export barriers. Notably, Kyrgyzstan will be able to supply potatoes to the Uzbek market without any limitations. This was confirmed during a meeting between Kyrgyz Deputy Minister Erlist Akunbekov and Uzbek Minister of Agriculture Ibrokhim Abdurakhmonov in Tashkent.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan to Cooperate on Snow Leopard Conservation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan will strengthen cooperation on preserving mountain ecosystems and the transboundary snow leopard population. The ministers discussed joint monitoring, data exchange, anti-poaching efforts, and protecting migration corridors. This collaboration will occur within the framework of the Global Snow Leopard and Ecosystem Protection Program.

item.title: Chinese Businesses Ready to Invest in Kazakhstan's 'People's Construction' Projects
item.description: Chinese companies from Shaanxi province are prepared to participate in Kazakh projects, ranging from oil refining in Atyrau to the construction of Alatau city. They expressed interest in the 'People's Construction' initiative announced by the President. Discussions also covered infrastructure modernization, AI development, and logistics.

item.title: Trade, Energy, and Investment: Saparov Discusses Key Issues with Putin in Moscow
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Saparov met with Russia's President Putin in Moscow to discuss trade, economic relations, energy, industry, finance, and education. Bilateral trade exceeded $4 billion in 2025, with nearly $3 billion in the first nine months of 2026. The Russian-Kyrgyz Development Fund has financed over 4,000 projects.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Security Services Arrest Two in Extortion Case
item.description: The State Committee for National Security (GKNB) in Kyrgyzstan has arrested two men in Sulyukta on suspicion of extorting 5 million soms from a coal mining company. The suspects allegedly demanded cash and coal, threatening to disrupt operations. One suspect is in custody, while the other's pre-trial measure is pending.

item.title: Hackers Linked to Kazakhstan Steal Over 2,000 Tajikistan Security Documents
item.description: Hackers suspected of links to Kazakhstan have stolen over 2,000 documents related to Tajikistan's security. A probe by Singapore's CloudSEK also found signs that the hackers accessed Uzbekistan's Smart Forestry platform, used in forest management. Further details were not immediately available.

item.title: Tajikistan to Assume CSTO Chairmanship in 2027, Emphasizing Mutual Trust
item.description: Tajikistan will assume the chairmanship of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) from Russia on January 1, 2027. President Emomali Rahmon stated that strengthening the CSTO must be based on mutual trust and consideration of member states' interests. Tajikistan plans to focus on regional security under the motto 'Collective Security: Strengthening Borders, Regional Resilience, Joint Responsibility'.

item.title: At Least 10 Police Officers Killed in Militant Attack in Pakistan
item.description: At least 10 police officers were killed when militants ambushed a convoy in Pakistan's Kohat district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, on November 11. Among the deceased were two senior officers. The attack occurred in a region bordering Afghanistan. A previous attack in the same district on September 18 resulted in 23 deaths.

item.title: 22 Afghan Prisoners Released in Libya and Repatriated to Afghanistan
item.description: At least 22 Afghan prisoners have been released in Libya and transferred to Afghanistan with the assistance of the Afghan embassy in Cairo. Efforts are ongoing to secure the release of other detained Afghans. However, the Taliban authorities have not disclosed the identities of those freed, the reasons for their detention, or the number of Afghans still imprisoned in Libya.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Calculating Loan Payments and Debt Burden on Family Budgets
item.description: Consumer loans are the most common in Kyrgyzstan, with outstanding debt exceeding 246.1 billion soms. This article explains how to calculate loan payments and assess the impact on a family's budget, considering housing, food, education, and unforeseen expenses. Interest rates vary, with commercial banks averaging 18.49% and MFIs reaching 29.64%.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine, and US Conclude Talks in Abu Dhabi Without Territorial Agreements
item.description: Trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the US concluded in Abu Dhabi, with an agreement reached only on the exchange of prisoners of war. While territorial issues were discussed, no progress was made. The main topic was a comprehensive European security system, which Russian officials noted is currently functioning poorly. Dialogue will continue.

item.title: Uzbek President proposes climate integration initiative at COP31 summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed a climate integration initiative at the COP31 World Leaders Summit in Antalya. He highlighted Uzbekistan's commitment to climate action, noting a 35% reduction in emissions per GDP unit and a new target of 50% by 2035. The President also detailed progress in water conservation and increasing green energy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Expand Trade and Economic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate Chairperson met with the President of the Korea Importers Association to discuss developing trade and economic ties. Discussions focused on exporting Uzbek products, particularly agricultural goods, to the Korean market and exploring a free trade agreement to boost bilateral trade. The importance of strengthening business ties and establishing joint ventures was emphasized.

item.title: Turkmenistan's TAPI Gas Pipeline Reaches Vicinity of Herat, Afghanistan
item.description: Turkmenistan announced its TAPI gas pipeline has reached the outskirts of Herat, Afghanistan. The first Afghan section is slated for completion by late 2026. Satellite imagery confirms pipeline construction approximately 22 kilometers west of Herat.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Major Production Complex for High-Voltage Electrical Equipment
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched a new high-tech production complex, 'NURA Electric,' in the Tashkent region, specializing in high and low-voltage electrical equipment. The facility aims to reduce import reliance, producing over 1,500 types of products with a 60% localization rate.

item.title: Uzbekistan Promotes Central Asian Integration Amid Climate Challenges
item.description: Uzbekistan is advocating for strengthened regional cooperation to address climate change impacts on water resources, agriculture, energy, and security. The nation emphasizes trust-based approaches, experience sharing, and joint initiatives. Climate integration, population protection, technological cooperation, and climate finance access were key topics at the COP31 session attended by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Ties with US Through Youth Educational Programs
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its international relations by fostering educational exchanges with the United States. A meeting in Washington focused on developing youth connections and organizing short-term educational programs for Uzbek students. Discussions included visits to leading universities and tech companies, aiming to broaden students' horizons in education, technology, and entrepreneurship.

item.title: US Exim Bank and DFC Decline Financing for Kazakhstan Tungsten Project
item.description: The US Export-Import Bank (EXIM) and the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) will not finance the Cove Kaz Capital Group's tungsten project in Kazakhstan. Bloomberg reports that Washington doubts the mines can be launched on schedule and fears proximity to China and Russia. Political disputes surrounding the Trump family's investments are also a factor.

item.title: Book on Mirziyoyev's Doctrine Launched in Seoul During Uzbek Delegation Visit
item.description: A Korean edition of the book "Mirziyoyev's Doctrine: Diplomacy of Opportunities in an Era of Global Instability" was presented in Seoul. The event, attended by Korean academics and business figures, highlighted Uzbekistan's reforms and foreign policy under President Mirziyoyev. The book covers Uzbekistan's foreign policy principles, regional cooperation, and international economic ties.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Attends COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov is attending the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change in Antalya, Turkey, on the President's instructions. The summit discusses global cooperation on sustainable development and climate change. Bektenov highlighted Kazakhstan's 'Clean Kazakhstan' initiative and afforestation efforts.

item.title: Central Asian nations seek to finalize business deals at Washington summit
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan sent high-level delegations to the B20 business summit in Washington, signaling a strong desire to finalize agreements with American businesses. Both nations expressed eagerness to move beyond rhetoric to concrete projects and mutually beneficial partnerships.

item.title: Turkmenistan Hosts International Investment Forum with Global Participation
item.description: Turkmenistan held an international investment forum in Ashgabat, attracting participants from Central Asia, the USA, UK, Japan, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, Germany, China, and France. The event focused on analyzing international standards for reducing methane emissions and improving the legal framework for the energy sector, aligning with national development priorities and the country's 'open door' policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Climate Integration Model for Central Asia
item.description: Uzbekistan has put forward an initiative to develop a Climate Integration Model for Central Asia. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced this at COP31, emphasizing that no single country can solve climate issues alone. He proposed three key areas for cooperation: information exchange, technological solutions, and financial mechanisms.
